approved_statement: Over Q(q) put Q=q², c=Q−1. Let Htilde_N have S_i²=c S_i+Q, braid/commuting relations, commuting invertible Y_j, S_i Y_j=Y_j S_i off the adjacent positions, and S_i Y_i S_i=Q Y_(i+1). Y_j multiplies the jth loop z, so u_(j−ae)=Y^a v_j; it is NOT z^-1. On fundamental residue tensors (j,k∈1,…,e), S_i sends (j,k) to −q(k,j) if j<k, to −(j,j) if j=k, and to −q(k,j)+(q²−1)(j,k) if j>k. For any Laurent polynomial f(Y), extend by S_i(f v)=s_i(f)S_i(v)+(1−q²)Y_(i+1)(f−s_i(f))/(Y_i−Y_(i+1)) v; the divided difference is a Laurent polynomial. This defines the action on all affine vectors. Equivalently the Leclerc generator t_i=−q^-1 S_i has roots q^-1,−q. A right-action notation uses the anti-involution fixing all generators, so products reverse operator order; the displayed matrices are unambiguous. The action commutes with the fixed U_q action (including total d). Put S_w by reduced words and A_N=Σ_(w∈S_N)S_w.
approved_strategy: This is the complete Leclerc§3.3–3.4 action, with S=−q t. For any integer l the Laurent divided difference is the finite geometric sum, giving S_i Y_i^l=Y_(i+1)^l S_i+(1−q²)Σ_(k=1)^l Y_i^(l−k)Y_(i+1)^k if l≥0; if l<0 use +(q²−1)Σ_(k=1)^(-l)Y_i^-k Y_(i+1)^(k+l). These formulas cover every loop shift. For the quadratic relation write S=S0 s+(1−Q)D, D=Y2(1−s)/(Y1−Y2): D²=−D and sD+Ds=1−s, together with S0²=(Q−1)S0+Q give S²=(Q−1)S+Q exactly. The braid identity is verified by expanding the three operators and clearing the three Laurent differences: the finite S0_i braid follows from the six strict orders and the repeated-index cases, and each remaining coefficient is the geometric divided-difference identity; distant actions commute. The Bernstein identity follows immediately from the l=1 formula and the quadratic equation. For U commutation, on colors i≠0 the two-vector matrices preserve the top/string/singlet blocks and K weights; on the0 color use its z-shifts and the same l=±1 Bernstein formulas. Off-adjacent tensor factors commute, so this proves each full generator identity. Total d commutes because each summand preserves total loop degree. This is a finite local matrix/divided-difference verification, not an unproved affine Schur-Weyl citation. KMS uses the OTHER parameter/coproduct: q_src=q^-1,K_src→K^-1, and its generator must be normalized accordingly; its unconverted formulas are not copied here.

before_definition:
Fix $e\ge2$ and keep all conventions of
[[def-the-level-one-vector-representation-its-affinization-and-energy-function]]:
the Cartan datum, the space $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q(q)u_m$
with $u_m=z^av_j$ ($m=j-ae$, $j\in\{1,\dots,e\}$), the operators
$K_h,E_i,F_i$, the classical weights $\lambda_j=\Lambda_j-\Lambda_{j-1}$, and the
fixed coproduct $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$,
$\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$,
$\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ of
[[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]].
Put $Q:=q^2$ and $c:=Q-1$, and let $Y_j$ denote the operator "multiply the $j$-th
tensor factor by $z$", so that $Y_j$ is invertible with
$Y_ju_m=u_{m-e}$ in the $j$-th slot and different $Y_j$ commute.

**The affine Hecke algebra $\tilde H_N$.** For $N\ge1$, $\tilde H_N$ is the
unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra with generators $S_1,\dots,S_{N-1}$ and invertible
$Y_1^{\pm1},\dots,Y_N^{\pm1}$ subject to

$$S_i^2=(Q-1)S_i+Q,\qquad S_iS_{i+1}S_i=S_{i+1}S_iS_{i+1},\qquad S_iS_j=S_jS_i\quad(|i-j|\ge2),$$

$$Y_iY_j=Y_jY_i,\qquad S_iY_j=Y_jS_i\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad S_iY_iS_i=QY_{i+1}.$$

The element $t_i:=-q^{-1}S_i$ then satisfies $(t_i-q)(t_i+q^{-1})=0$; for a
reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}\in S_N$ put $S_w:=S_{i_1}\cdots S_{i_k}$
and $A_N:=\sum_{w\in S_N}S_w$ (well defined by the braid relations).

**The two-vector operator and its extension.** On residue tensors
$v_j\otimes v_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,\dots,e\}$) set

$$S(v_j\otimes v_k)=\begin{cases}-q\,v_k\otimes v_j,&j<k,\\ -\,v_j\otimes v_j,&j=k,\\ -q\,v_k\otimes v_j+(Q-1)v_j\otimes v_k,&j>k.\end{cases}$$

For a Laurent monomial $f=Y_1^pY_2^q$ define, with $s(f):=Y_2^pY_1^q$ the
swap of the two loop variables,

$$S(f\,w):=s(f)\,S(w)+(1-Q)\,Y_2\,\frac{f-s(f)}{Y_1-Y_2}\,w\qquad(w\in V\otimes V),$$

and extend linearly; the quotient $(f-s(f))/(Y_1-Y_2)$ is a Laurent polynomial,
so $S$ is a well-defined linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes V_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
On $V_{\mathrm{aff}}^{\otimes N}$ the generator $S_i$ acts by this operator on
the tensor factors $i,i+1$ and $Y_j$ acts on the $j$-th factor as above; this
defines the **affine Hecke action**.
